body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutamekasamaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma karīramaṇḍale ca / atha khalvāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nekavidyādharakoṭīniyutaśatasahastrastreṇa parivṛto yena bhagavāṃstenopasamakrāmat / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyaekānte nyasīda bhagavantametadavocat / idaṃ mama bhagavannekādaśamukhaṃ nāma hṛdayamekādaśabhiḥ kalpakoṭībhirbhāṣitam / ahaṃ cettarhi bhāṣiṣyāmi sarvasattvānāmarthāya hitāya sukhāya sarvavyādhipraśamanāya sarvapāpālakṣmiduḥsvapnapratinivāraṇāya sarvākālamṛtyupratinivāraṇāya aprasādānāṃ prasādanāya sarvavighnavināyakānāṃ praśamanāya / nāhaṃ bhagavan samanupaśyāmi (

children.text: ) sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyā yadanena hṛdayena rakṣe kṛte paritre parigrahe śāntisvastyayane daṇḍaparihare śastraparihare viṣaprahāṇe kṛte yaḥ kaścidatikramet na praśamet nedaṃsthānaṃ vidyate sthāptya paurāṇāṃ karma vipacyate / tadasya ca kalpayato 'bhiśraddadhataḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyati / sarvabuddhastutaḥ samanvāhṛto 'yaṃ hṛdayaṃ sarvatathāgatānumodito 'yaṃ hṛdayam / smarāmyahaṃ bhagavan gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ pareṇa śatapadmanayanacūḍapratihataraṅgavelakiraṇarājasya nāma tathāgatasya / mayā tathāgatasyāntike śrutamayaṃ hṛdayam udgṛhītaṃca / saha pratilaṃbhena daśasu dikṣu sarvatathāgatāḥ (
children.translated_text: in this world with its <s>devas</s>, its <s>Māra</s>, its <s>Brahmā</s>, among the populace with its ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, anyone who could transgress or not be pacified when protection has been made with this <s>hṛdaya</s>, when a safeguard has been made, a shelter, a rite of peace and well-being, a warding off of punishment, a warding off of weapons, and an elimination of poison — such a case does not exist, except for the ripening of past <s>karma</s>. And for one who practices it and has faith in it, absolutely nothing [harmful] will come to pass. This <s>hṛdaya</s> has been praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>, this <s>hṛdaya</s> has been attended to, and this <s>hṛdaya</s> has been approved by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. O Blessed One, I remember: beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śatapadmanayanacūḍapratihataraṅgavelakiraṇarāja</s>. By me, in the presence of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, this <s>hṛdaya</s> was heard and taken up. Immediately upon receiving it, all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions

children.text: ) sumukhībhūtā anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilabdhāḥ / evaṃ bahukaro 'yaṃ hṛdayam tasmāttarhi śrāddhena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā satkṛtyāyaṃ hṛdayaṃ sādhayitavyam / ananyamanasā nityaṃ sādhayitavyam / kalyamutthāya aṣṭottaravāraśataṃ pravartayitavyam / ddaṣṭadharmikā guṇā daśa parigrahītavyāḥ / katame daśa / yaduta nirvyādhirbhaviṣyati / sarvatathāgataiḥ parigṛhītaśca bhaviṣyati / dhanadhānyahiraṇyābharaṇamasya akṣayaṃ bhaviṣyati / sarvaśatravo vaśyā avamarditā bhaviṣyanti / rājasabhāyāṃ prathamamālapitavyaṃ maṃsyati / na viṣaṃ na garaṃ na jvaraṃ na śastraṃ kāye kramiṣyati / nodakena kālaṃ kariṣyati / nāgninā kālaṃ kariṣyati / nākālamṛtyunā kālaṃca kariṣyati / apare cattvāro guṇānuśaṃsā udgrahīṣyati / maraṇakāle tathāgatadarśanaṃ bhaviṣyati / na cāpāyepūpapatsyate / naviṣamāparihāreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati / itścyutaḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyate /
children.translated_text: became well-disposed and attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (the acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). So greatly beneficial is this <s>hṛdaya</s>. Therefore, a faithful son or daughter of good family should respectfully practice this <s>hṛdaya</s>. It should be practiced constantly with undivided mind. Rising early, it should be recited one hundred and eight times. Ten benefits visible in this very life are to be obtained. What are these ten? One will be free from disease. One will be protected by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. One's wealth, grain, gold, and ornaments will be inexhaustible. All enemies will be subdued and vanquished. One will be deemed worthy of being addressed first in the royal court. Neither poison, nor harmful substances, nor fever, nor weapons will afflict the body. One will not die by water. One will not die by fire. One will not die by untimely death. Furthermore, four additional benefits and rewards will be obtained: at the time of death, there will be a vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; one will not be reborn in the lower realms; one will not die through unfortunate circumstances; and, having departed from this life, one will be reborn in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss).

body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Karīramaṇḍala</s>. Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>Mahāsattva</s>), surrounded by an assembly of many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-holders), approached the Blessed One. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, having circumambulated the Blessed One, he sat down at one side and said this to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, this <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī) of mine called 'Eleven-Faced' has been spoken over eleven <s>koṭīs</s> (ten millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). I shall now speak it for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all beings, for the pacification of all diseases, for the warding off of all evil, misfortune, and bad dreams, for the warding off of all untimely death, for the gladdening of the unfaithful, and for the pacification of all obstacles and hindrances. O Blessed One, I do not see

body.text: smarāmyahaṃ bhagavanniti daśānāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ kalpānāṃ tataḥ pareṇa paratareṇa mandāravagandho nāma tathāgato 'bhūt / tatra mayā gṛhaparibhūtenāyamudgṛhītam / cattvāriṃśat kalpasahastrāṇi saṃsārāḥ paścānmukhīkṛtāḥ / eṣa ca mayā hṛdayaṃ pravartitvā sarvasmin karuṇāyanajñānagarbhabodhisattvavimokṣaṃ (

children.text: ) buddhabodhirbhaviṣyati / bhagavānāha / sādhu sādhu kulaputra yat sarvasattvānāmantike evaṃrūpā mahākaruṇā / śakṣyasi tvaṃ kulaputraḥ anenopāyena sarvasattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayitum / udgṛhītaṃ camayā hṛdayamanumoditam / bhāṣadhvaṃ kulaputra / tataḥ khalvāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattva utthāyasanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅga kṛtvā bhagavataścaraṇayoḥ praṇipatya idaṃ hṛdayamāvartayati sma /
children.translated_text: ). The <s>Bhagavat</s> said: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! Such great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward all sentient beings! You, son of good family, will be able by this means to establish all sentient beings in unsurpassed perfect awakening. The <s>hṛdaya</s> has been received by me and approved. Please recite it, O son of good family.' Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and bowing at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, recited this <s>hṛdaya</s>:

body.translated_text: O Blessed One, I remember: beyond and further beyond <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of ten <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mandāravagandha</s>. There, while I was still a householder, this [<s>hṛdaya</s>] was taken up by me. Forty thousand <s>kalpas</s> of <s>saṃsāra</s> were turned away. And having set this <s>hṛdaya</s> in motion, in all [realms] the liberation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [known as] the <s>Karuṇāyanajñānagarbha</s> (Womb of Compassionate Wisdom)

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / namo vairocanāya tathāgatāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / namaḥ atītānāgatapratyutpannebhyaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo 'rhad bhyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels). Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s>. Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One. Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, future, and present.

body.text: omdhara dhara / dhiri dhiri / dhuru dhuru / iṭṭe viṭṭe / cale cale / pracale pracale / kusume kusumavare / ili mili viṭi svāhā / evaṃ mūlamantraḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ dhara dhara / dhiri dhiri / dhuru dhuru / iṭṭe viṭṭe / cale cale / pracale pracale / kusume kusumavare / ili mili viṭi svāhā</s>. Thus is the root <s>mantra</s> (<s>mūlamantra</s>).

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya / tad yathā hāhā hāhā / ime tile cile bhile khile svāhā / snānopasparśanavastrābhyukṣipaṇamantraḥ saptajāpena / (
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>. Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>. That is to say: <s>hā hā hā hā / ime tile cile bhile khile svāhā</s>. This is the <s>mantra</s> for bathing, sprinkling, and offering garments—to be recited seven times. (

body.text:
namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāyamahāsattvāya /
tadyathā ṭuru ṭuru hā hā hā hā svāhā / dhūpadīpanivedanamantraḥ /
body.translated_text:
Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>. Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>.
That is to say: <s>ṭuru ṭuru hā hā hā hā svāhā</s>. This is the <s>mantra</s> for offering incense and lamps.

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāyā mahāsattvāyā / tadyathā thiri thiri dhiri dhiri svāhā / gandhapuṣpopanivedanamantraḥ /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>. Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>. That is to say: <s>thiri thiri dhiri dhiri svāhā</s>. This is the <s>mantra</s> for offering perfume and flowers.

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvaraya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / tadyathā sāde sāde sidi sidi sudu sudu svāhā / balinivedanamantra ekaviṃśatijāpena /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>. Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One. That is to say: <s>sāde sāde sidi sidi sudu sudu svāhā</s>. This is the <s>mantra</s> for offering food (<s>bali</s>)—to be recited twenty-one times.

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāyabodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya / mahākāruṇikāya / tadyathā yasi ddhasi cari huru icuruḥ suruḥ muruḥ svāhā / homamantraḥ / anena mantreṇa jñātīnāṣṭai(?) ragniṃ prajvālya dadhimadhudhṛtābhyaktānāmahorātrauṣikena ekena triṃśatā homaḥ kāryaḥ / tataḥ karma samārabhet /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>. Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One. That is to say: <s>yasi ddhasi cari huru icuruḥ suruḥ muruḥ svāhā</s>. This is the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) <s>mantra</s>. With this <s>mantra</s>, having lit the [...] fire for one's relatives, with [fuel] anointed with curds, honey, and ghee, one should perform thirty <s>homas</s> in a day and night. Then one should commence the ritual.

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / tadyathā ili mili tili tili hili svāhā / dīpābaddha udakena+ +rvā bhasmanā vā saptajāpena /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s>. Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the Great Compassionate One. That is to say: <s>ili mili tili tili hili svāhā</s>. [This mantra is to be used] with a lamp, with water, [...] or with ashes—to be recited seven times.

body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / tadyathā piṭi piṭi tiṭi tiṭi viṭi viṭi gaccha gaccha bhagavānāryāvalokiteśvara svabhavanaṃ svabhavanaṃ svāhā / udake saptavārān parijapya caturdiśaṃ kṣipet / āryāvalokiteśvara gaccha svabhavanam /
body.translated_text: Homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>)! Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being (<s>Mahāsattva</s>), the greatly compassionate one (<s>Mahākāruṇika</s>)! The <s>mantra</s> is as follows: <s>piṭi piṭi tiṭi tiṭi viṭi viṭi gaccha gaccha</s> — O Blessed <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s>, [return] to your own abode, to your own abode! <s>Svāhā</s>! Having recited [this mantra] seven times over water, one should cast it in the four directions. O noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, go to your own abode.
